_comment_hooks: SessionStart fires on startup, resume, and after compaction. The compaction case is the important one: compaction silently drops CLAUDE.md and the constitution, and an agent that has forgotten its invariants will violate all thirty without noticing. This re-injects them.

hooks.command: echo '--- CONTEXT REPAIR AFTER COMPACTION ---'; cat CLAUDE.md; echo; echo '--- CONSTITUTION ---'; cat docs/CONSTITUTION.md; echo; echo '--- CURRENT PHASE ---'; grep -m1 -A3 'Current phase' CLAUDE.md; echo; echo '--- LAST 3 PROGRESS ENTRIES ---'; tail -n 60 ops/PROGRESS.md; echo; echo '--- OPEN QUESTIONS (ask, do not decide) ---'; grep -E '^\*\*OQ-' docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md
echo 'Run /session-start before any implementation work.'; git log --oneline -5

_comment_permissions: Joe's standing instruction: 'i dont want to keep having to press accept.' The answer is not to disable permissions — it is to pre-approve everything reversible so that a prompt actually means something when it appears. Everything in allow is local and undoable. Everything in deny is unrecoverable and is blocked outright rather than prompted, because a prompt you see fifty times a day is a prompt you stop reading.
_comment_pretooluse: The destructive-command guard. This is not paranoia: in July 2025 a coding agent deleted a production database during a change freeze and then generated 4,000 fabricated records to cover the gap.
